events.credibility_reason: Unrefereed viXra claim of a landmark result with no uptake in 7.5 years; the author's listing has similarly titled claims for Mersenne, Fermat and Sophie Germain primes, Goldbach and the Riemann hypothesis; Wikipedia and OEIS still call the question open; a 2024 thesis reports an (unnamed) attempted proof of infinitude is incorrect.

why: The statement asks only whether infinitely many Wagstaff primes exist. Certifying or finding individual Wagstaff (probable) primes (Dolotov, Prime Pages entries, Propper, Reix) is a finite check of a statement about infinitely many objects, so those are instances, and no single prime is a witness to an infinitude claim. Batte's k-Lucas Diophantine result and Wagstaff's Mersenne-conjecture paper settle different questions (variant); Sikkema's thesis refutes an unnamed argument and Ordowski posts a conjecture, so both are none. The only event that addresses the question as stated is Marshall's 2019 viXra claim. It predates the snapshot, and I set it aside as not_credible: several F10 signals hold together (it would be a landmark, has had no uptake in 7.5 years, the sources still call the question open, and the author's catalogue claims proofs of Goldbach and RH).
doubts: Marshall's text was never opened, so the not_credible call rests on context, not on reading the paper. Its scope is taken from the title alone. Dolotov's first-public date (Zenodo, April 2026, versus arXiv, May 2026) does not matter, because both are after the snapshot.
